answer: Persistent-work memory ledger. Each identity must solve a randomly issued cipher over its own accumulating transaction history before its next action is accepted, and the solution cost grows with how little history it has. An honest agent amortizes work across a long orchard of past actions; a fresh clone pays full price every time. Sustained participation also requires a copper-denominated deposit released only after long-lived activity, making mass cloning costlier than one honest lineage.
